{"consolidated_memory":"**Off-by-one day issues in ui/components/DatePicker.tsx — Two separate incidents**

**OCCASION 1: 2026-04-23**
- File/component: ui/components/DatePicker.tsx
- Problem: Off-by-one day error in date picker, specific to users in negative UTC offset timezones
- Signal: Selected value appeared one day behind the displayed label
- Root cause: Clock skew between two hosts
- Fix: Switched the deadline calculation to use a monotonic clock (PR #5537 on branch fix/off-by-one-day-1)
- Reproduction: Pick the first of the month and reopen the date picker
- Outcome: Stopped 9 duplicate rows per day from being written to the database

**OCCASION 2: 2026-07-05**
- File/component: ui/components/DatePicker.tsx (same component, same corner as earlier work)
- Problem: Off-by-one day error in date picker, specific to deeply nested input fields beyond six levels deep
- Signal: Selected value appeared one day behind the displayed label
- Root cause: Missing composite database index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: Added the composite index and backfilled data in batches (PR #5599 on branch fix/off-by-one-day-2)
- Reproduction: Pick the first of the month and reopen the date picker
- Outcome: Reclaimed 40 GB of blob storage

These are distinct bugs with the same symptom but different triggers and solutions: one related to timezone/clock handling, the other to database indexing."}
